prompt:
Approach this as a Ecologist. Sees community dynamics, niches, competition, diversity indices, and succession. Bring that lens to the problem.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Hysteresis test of AP-1 state after stimulus removal (priming/succession)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or wounding), then withdraw it and track AP-1 factor composition (FOS/JUN family), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and re-challenge transcriptional response over days to weeks. Like ecological succession, memory means the post-stimulus state differs from naive and shows a faster or larger response, or path dependence on stimulus history.

ideas.title: AP-1 family 'community composition' and diversity indices across time and cell states
ideas.description: Use single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) and CUT&RUN or ChIP for each FOS/JUN/ATF member to quantify the relative abundance of AP-1 dimers at enhancers. Compute Shannon/Simpson diversity and beta-diversity (turnover) of AP-1 composition between naive, stimulated, and recovered cells to see whether a persistent compositional shift (a new stable community) marks memory.

ideas.title: Competitive niche occupancy at shared enhancers by AP-1 versus other pioneer factors
ideas.description: Map footprinting and motif occupancy of AP-1 relative to competing factors (e.g., CTCF, lineage TFs, NF-κB, glucocorticoid receptor) at memory-associated enhancers, and perturb AP-1 dosage using degron or dominant-negative (A-FOS) to see if niches are lost or taken over. Competitive release or displacement would show whether AP-1 holds the site open and excludes rivals, thereby maintaining memory.

ideas.title: Acute degron removal after the priming window (keystone-removal experiment)
ideas.description: Deplete AP-1 (dTAG/auxin degron on FOS, JUN, or by A-FOS) either during priming or only during the memory interval, then re-stimulate. If memory persists after AP-1 loss in the interval, AP-1 is only an initiator. If it collapses, AP-1 actively maintains memory, much like removing a keystone species. Pair this with ATAC and histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) to separate chromatin-based from TF-based persistence.

ideas.title: Lineage-tracked single-cell heritability and mathematical model of state persistence
ideas.description: Use barcoded lineage tracing or live reporters (AP-1 activity reporter, FOS-GFP) to measure whether AP-1 state is inherited across divisions versus rewired by noise. Compare sister-cell correlation to random pairs. Fit bistability or positive-feedback population models (analogous to alternative stable states in ecology) to estimate persistence half-life, and test predictions by perturbing feedback loops such as FOS/JUN autoregulation.
